question: The aim of the Permanent Settlement Act of 1793 was to enter into an agreement for fixed revenue collection between the East India Company and _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Landlords**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Permanent Settlement Act of 1793 was introduced by the British East India Company under the leadership of Lord Cornwallis.
 
• This act aimed to create a fixed revenue system by entering into agreements with landlords (Zamindars) for revenue collection.
 
• The landlords were responsible for collecting taxes from the peasants and paying a fixed amount to the Company.
 
• It was intended to stabilize revenue collection and ensure a steady income for the British administration.
 
• Landlords were given hereditary rights over the land, which they could pass on to their descendants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindari System**

 
 
• The Zamindari System was a traditional system where landlords (Zamindars) collected taxes from peasants.
 
• Under this system, Zamindars were recognized as landowners by the British government.
 
• The system aimed to create a class of loyal landlords who would support British rule.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Settlement**
 
 
• Revenue Settlement refers to the agreement made between the British government and landlords for tax collection.
 
• It ensured that the government received a fixed amount of revenue annually.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Peasants**
 
 
• Peasants were often exploited as landlords sought to maximize revenue collection.
 
• Many peasants faced high taxes and were at risk of losing their land.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Settlement Act**
 
 
• The act was part of the larger framework of British colonial administration in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for the modern land revenue system in Bengal and later extended to other parts of India.
